title: Migration minister reveals significant crackdown on illegal immigration as well as a raft of measures including shutting down IPAS centres - but it will also make life difficult for some Ukrainians fl
summary:
The Government has signalled a significant crackdown on illegal immigration this year, promising to reduce the number of IPAS centres and ratchet up the number of chartered deportation flights.
Writing in today’s Irish Mail on Sunday, Migration Minister Colm Brophy said he and Justice Minister Jim O’Callaghan will ‘reduce rather than increase the number of IPAS centres this year’.
During this period, the number of emergency accommodation centres rose from just 25 in December 2021 to 259 in January this year.
At its peak last year, there were a total of 33,000 asylum seekers in 313 State-owned and commercial accommodation centres who stayed an average of 24.3 months.
And he confirmed plans for new legislation to ensure asylum seekers who obtain employment while living in IPAS centres will pay rent to offset accommodation costs.
